source.title: Aperiodic neural timescales in prefrontal cortex dilate with increased task abstraction

confidence_rationale: Deliberately low. A preprint with no stated sample size in the abstract, using EEG-derived aperiodic autocorrelation as a proxy for integration window. Included because it is the only source found that bears on whether the integration window is a FIXED parameter or an actively-set one -- which is a direct methodological challenge to MECH-021's discriminative pair. Weak evidence, but it bears on a design decision no other entry touches.
failure_signatures: Neural timescales dilate with task demand rather than being fixed structural constants, so MECH-021's arm design (theta_buffer_size fixed at 1 versus 10 for the run) tests a narrower proposition than the claim states: whether a fixed-wide window beats a fixed-narrow one, not whether an appropriately-set window beats a badly-set one.

If the biological window is adaptive, a REE substrate that cannot adapt its window may show a flat anticipatory-restraint fraction for reasons having nothing to do with whether 'now' is a control surface -- producing a FALSIFYING result that is actually an artefact of the fixed-buffer implementation.

Aperiodic autocorrelation decay measured from scalp EEG is several inferential steps from a functional integration window; the finding may reflect changes in excitation-inhibition balance rather than in the width of any integrated present.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Aperiodic neural timescales, estimated from the autocorrelation function of the aperiodic (non-oscillatory) component of human EEG, dilate over prefrontal cortical regions as the abstraction of task-relevant contextual information increases.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-021 treats the width of 'now' as the manipulated variable and the anticipatory-restraint fraction as the outcome. Cellier et al. suggest the width is itself an OUTPUT of control rather than a fixed input to it: prefrontal integration windows expand when the task requires holding more abstract context. Read charitably this strengthens the claim's spirit -- the temporal window really is part of the control apparatus, not inert plumbing. Read strictly it complicates the falsifier, because REE fixes theta_buffer_size per arm and therefore cannot express the adaptive setting that the biology appears to use.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is a preprint, and the inferential chain from scalp-EEG aperiodic autocorrelation decay to 'width of the integrated present' is long: the measure is also sensitive to excitation-inhibition balance, and the abstract does not state a sample size. The direction of causation is unresolved -- timescales may dilate BECAUSE more context is held, rather than dilating in order to hold it -- and only the latter reading supports the control-surface framing. Treat as a design caveat on MECH-021's falsifier, not as evidence for or against the claim's substance.
mapping.source_context: Human scalp EEG during a cognitive-control task manipulating the abstraction level of task-relevant context; aperiodic component isolated from oscillatory confounds; no aversive or avoidance component.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality held low: unrefereed preprint, no sample size in the abstract, and a proxy measure whose interpretation is contested. Transfer risk raised above the other entries because the causal direction of the effect is unresolved and only one direction supports the control-surface reading.
